To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and analyzed an open real-time architecture for distributed systems.

we have designed an open real-time system architecture for distributed systems with hard real-time applications and non-real-time applications, and that the architecture is schedulable and has been implemented in a real-time system.

the proposed architecture provides the following benefits: 1) the system is schedulable as long as the sum of the reserved CPU utilizations of all real-time applications is less than 100% of CPU utilization, and 2) the real-time applications are independent from the non-real-time applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, analysis, and implementation of a real-time environment architecture that is open to the deployment of applications with hard real-time constraints and applications with non-real-time constraints.
(1) The design of an open real-time architecture that allows a set of real-time applications to be deployed and executed concurrently in the same distributed system.
the design of a general real-time environment that supports a wide range of applications and is suitable for distributed real-time systems.

the proposed open environment can guarantee all hard real-time tasks to have their reserved resources.
the proposed architecture is a promising approach for open real-time systems.
our proposed open real-time environment provides a simple and flexible solution to scheduling hard real-time applications in a complex distributed system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a real-time environment architecture with a provably correct two-level scheduling scheme for distributed real-time systems with open environments.
we have developed a real-time environment architecture, which is open and scalable, and which can guarantee the real-time properties of the applications in the system.
we propose an open environment architecture for real-time systems, which allows the development of real-time applications independently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can guarantee real-time applications to meet their deadlines in an environment where other applications can be added or deleted dynamically.
the system-wide scheduler can be implemented as a simple and efficient priority scheduler, which makes it easy to implement and deploy in real systems.
we can use a two-level scheduling architecture to guarantee the real-time performance of all real-time applications running in a system.
